purpose: Source approval rules for TuneVault audio discovery and review. A title match alone never approves a recording. There is no manual per-tune genre/style review — exact title/alias match plus rights/license and a verified playable file are the bar for auto-attaching.

sources.name: Slippery Hill
requirements: Exact title or stored-alias filename evidence, or a live canonical source page that proves both its heading and direct audio link
HTTPS, audio MIME type, bounded response, and recognizable audio signature verification immediately before apply
No replacement of an existing trusted direct recording or Library of Congress reference
sources.context: Performer and edition details are retained when the source page provides them. Discovery/apply run against the full unresolved backlog by default (no small fixed batch limit).

sources.name: Internet Archive
requirements: Exact title or stored-alias evidence on an individual audio file name or file title; collection titles alone are not sufficient
Current collection metadata must provide a named creator and either rights or a license URL
HTTPS, audio MIME type, bounded response, and recognizable audio signature verification immediately before apply
No replacement of an existing trusted direct recording or Library of Congress reference
sources.context: Review reports preserve the collection, file, rights/license, creator, performer when named, and source-page URL. There is no manual editorial 'is this a genuine old-time edition' gate — exact match, rights/license, attribution, and a verified playable file are sufficient to auto-attach. Discovery/apply run against the full unresolved backlog by default (no small fixed batch limit).

sources.name: Wikimedia Commons
requirements: Exact title or stored-alias match against the Commons file page title (e.g. File:<Tune Title>.ogg)
An explicit declared license or usage-terms string on the file page that does not read as restricted/fair-use, plus a named artist or credit line
HTTPS, audio (or application/ogg container) MIME type, bounded response, and recognizable audio signature verification immediately before apply
No replacement of an existing trusted direct recording or Library of Congress reference
sources.context: Commons only hosts freely licensed or public-domain media, but individual files can still declare restricted terms, so the license line is rechecked live before every apply.

sources.name: Library of Congress
sources.status: approved as a trusted archival reference
requirements: Exact item-title or verified alias match in a named public collection
A stable Library of Congress item reference
Do not label a reference as a direct downloadable player URL until that playback path is separately verified
sources.context: LOC records remain distinct from direct-audio coverage in catalog audits. The loc.gov API/search endpoints were not reachable from the automated sourcing environment during the most recent large-scale pass, so no new direct-audio LOC lane was added; existing LOC references are unaffected.

sources.name: Southern Folklife Collection / Digital SFC
sources.status: evaluated, not approved for automated direct imports
requirements: Needs a source-specific, stable per-file playback and rights verification lane before use
sources.context: The collection contains relevant field recordings, but search discovery alone is not enough evidence for automatic attachment. No lawful, scriptable per-file audio+rights endpoint was found during evaluation.

sources.name: Smithsonian Folkways / Learning Lab
sources.status: evaluated, not approved for automated direct imports
requirements: Needs full-track (not preview-clip) audio under a clear open license before it can be auto-attached
sources.context: The Smithsonian Open Access API returns rich catalog metadata for Folkways recordings but no downloadable audio file for them (they are physical/commercial recordings, not digitized open-access media). Folkways.si.edu track pages offer short promotional preview clips only, sold under standard commercial terms rather than a redistributable license, so they do not clear the rights bar.

sources.name: Folkstreams / NCTA
sources.status: evaluated, not approved for automated direct imports
requirements: Needs a documented public API or file listing that maps individual tune titles to a direct, rights-cleared audio/video file
sources.context: Folkstreams publishes documentary films (not individual tune tracks), and the site exposes no discoverable API for scripted per-title lookup, so exact tune-title matching and rights verification are not currently possible here.

sources.name: Digital Library of Appalachia
sources.status: evaluated, not approved for automated direct imports
requirements: Needs a reachable, scriptable per-item metadata/rights endpoint before use
sources.context: The site runs on CONTENTdm; its dmwebservices API endpoint returned 403/blocked responses to automated requests during evaluation, and per-item rights statements vary by collection, so this lane cannot be verified end-to-end from the automated sourcing environment.

sources.name: Duke Digital Collections
sources.status: evaluated, not approved for automated direct imports
requirements: Needs a reachable, scriptable per-item metadata/rights endpoint before use
sources.context: repository.duke.edu is protected by an interactive bot challenge that blocks scripted access, so item-level title, rights, and audio-file verification cannot be automated from this environment.
